dct_description_sm: What form the polar landscape will take in the near future will depend on the balance of competing forces - increased ice-wedge thermokarst versus the stabilizing effect of increasing vegetation cover in high latitudes, both of which are predicted by global warming. This balance remains unclear. The goal of the 2012-2013 dataset was to characterize the effects of climate induced thermokarst on the ice-wedge thermal regime, near-surface active layer dynamics, and vegetation community structure. Two different thermokarst sites were selected within a 25km distance from Eureka, Nunavut   a drained thaw pond and a basin that has formed through advanced thermokarst. Each site was assessed and data collected on vegetation richness and percent cover, soil properties, and permafrost active layer characteristics. The data and analyses of this study will provide a new framework to conceptualize the effects of climate change on far northern ecosystems.
dct_title_s: Vegetation, soil, and permafrost data collected from a thermokarst basin and a drained thaw pond on Ellesmere Island, Nunavut
